prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell), system-of-interest, coordinates Meridian International Airport, Harbor East Airport, North Valley Airport, Lakeside Regional Airport, Southport Airport; combines regional flow management/Airport Collaborative Decision-Making.
Planning: Demand Prediction Service consumes schedules, Flight Intent Message, recovery plans/changes; Capacity Assessment Module assesses weather/runways/sectors/resources; Slot Allocation Engine allocates fairly/traceably; Airport CDM Portal shares readiness/confirms decisions; Digital Briefing Room supports collaboration.
Tactical: Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, Departure Metering Service, Arrival Regulation Console, Contingency Operations Console execute coordination.
Integration: Weather Ingest Gateway, Flight Data Exchange, Surface Surveillance Adapter, Airline Interface Adapter supply feeds; Alert Distribution Hub.
Governance: Performance Analytics Warehouse, Audit Event Ledger, Identity Access Service, Business Rules Registry, Time Synchronization Service.
Connected indicators: North Runway Meter, South Runway Meter, East Apron Sensor, West Apron Sensor, Sector Load Monitor, Gate Conflict Detector.
Actors: Regional Flow Manager leads balancing; Airline Operations Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Aircraft Operator Representative, Slot Coordinator align intentions/schedules/slots; Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Airport Duty Manager, Ground Handling Dispatcher, Deicing Coordinator represent local operations; Meteorology Briefing Officer, Airspace Sector Planner, Military Airspace Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator address capacity constraints; Data Governance Steward, System Support Engineer maintain quality/access/continuity/configuration.
Participants: scheduled passenger/cargo/charter/based airlines; airport-approved handlers/fueling/deicing/towing/passenger-transport/ramp providers.
External: reservation/crew/baggage/commercial systems, national surveillance infrastructure, aircraft avionics. Boundary interfaces only validate identity, receive authorized data, publish approved information, preserve auditability; statutory/local command remains external.
Normal Operations: constraints propagate delays/reduce Airport Acceptance Rate. Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State: must rapidly develop Tactical Regulation Proposal, consistently communicate Ground Delay Program. Recovery Phase: must restore scheduled flow, monitor Target Off Block Time, Calculated Takeoff Time, Slot Compliance State.
Common Situation Display should share demand/capacity/constraints/measures with authorized users; Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger should preserve rationale/timing/authorization.

Document units:
S045: Air navigation service participation includes regional flow management personnel, tower supervisory personnel, airspace planning personnel, and any designated military coordination function that affects civil capacity planning.
S046: The shared operational picture includes Flight Intent Message status, Airport Capacity Plan assumptions, Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, Airport Acceptance Rate constraints, Common Situation Display content, Tactical Regulation Proposal status, Collaborative Decision Log entries, and Post Operations Report outputs.
S047: The system boundary explicitly covers Normal Operations, Adverse Weather Mode, Capacity Reduction State, Recovery Phase, Contingency Fallback State, and Slot Compliance State because these states drive stakeholder participation and operating procedures.
S048: Participation in the regional system requires each stakeholder organization to assign accountable representatives, maintain current contact details, follow agreed data use rules, and support post-operational review of decisions made through the Regional Flow Platform.
S049: The daily planning cycle begins with a pre-tactical baseline prepared each morning before the main bank structure is locked for operational use.
S050: The Regional Flow Manager owns the baseline process and confirms that the planning horizon, cutover time, and review checkpoints are understood by the participating operational roles.
S051: The Regional Flow Platform creates the initial demand picture from published schedules, approved seasonal allocations, overnight schedule changes, and received Flight Intent Message data.
S052: The Flight Data Exchange normalizes flight identifiers, aircraft types, routing fields, and planned operating times so that later comparisons use a single reference record.
S053: The Demand Prediction Service converts the normalized schedule into expected arrival and departure demand by time band, runway direction, terminal area, and major traffic flow.
S054: The Airline Operations Coordinator reviews material deviations from filed intent, including aircraft swaps, early cancellations, recovery flights, and known connection protection actions.
S055: The Aircraft Operator Representative validates that operator priorities are visible where they are allowed by the Business Rules Registry and local coordination agreements.
S056: The Meteorology Briefing Officer provides the morning weather outlook with emphasis on wind trend, ceiling, visibility, convective risk, temperature limits, and confidence over the planning horizon.
S057: The Weather Ingest Gateway makes the outlook available to the Capacity Assessment Module and preserves the forecast issue time for audit and later performance review.
S058: The Airspace Sector Planner declares expected sector constraints, route availability assumptions, and any planned staffing limitations that could influence arrival or departure metering.
